newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Nayarit state sees '96 mining output up.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Nayarit state sees '96 mining output up.

text.p: Precious and base metals output in Mexico's western state of Nayarit is seen ending the year around 15 percent higher than output in 1995, a state government mining source said Tuesday.
Sergio Andrade Blanco, of Nararit's Mineral Resources Council, said gold, silver, copper, lead and zinc output would all rise this year.

"Mining output has prospered from the presence of both foreign and national companies...," Andrade said. He added that the increase in production could be greater once more projects go through into exploitation stages from exploration.
Nayarit, not one of Mexico's foremost mining zones, produced 176.04 kg of gold in 1995, 4,446.8 kg of silver, 12.3 tonnes of copper, 10.2 tonnes of lead and 6.2 tonnes of zinc.
